The percentile version is clearly worse (+0.0133), so the plain level of the range is the right measure. Two attempts in a row have now failed to beat the 5-day average by 0.002, so I'll stop and hand in that one.

What I found: the daily high-low range does carry information in the direction the idea states — coins with a wide range subsequently do slightly worse, and the effect survives removal of liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum, with incremental IC +0.0203 (t = 8.7) and the same sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. Averaging the range over 10 days instead of 5 gave a slightly weaker result (+0.0186), and ranking the range inside its own 20-day window cut it to +0.0133, so the plain level of the range over a short window is the version to keep.

The idea is about where the close sits inside the day's range: a coin closing near its high means buyers dominated that day. That ratio is unit-free, so it compares across coins. I'll start with the plainest form — the close-to-high ratio averaged over 5 days — before adding any smoothing.

rank IC: +0.0030
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0079 (t = 3.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0054, 2023 +0.0112, 2024 +0.0058

The plain 5-day average is already positive in the direction the idea predicts, with a t of 3.1 and all three sub-periods positive. Since the daily ratio is noisy, I'll average it over a longer window to see whether the signal is more stable rather than a short-lived blip.

rank IC: +0.0096
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0021 (t = 0.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0009, 2023 +0.0002, 2024 +0.0047

Averaging over 20 days destroys the signal (+0.0021, t=0.7), so the effect lives in recent days, not in slow drift. I'll keep the short window but make each daily ratio robust to single-day outliers by replacing the mean with a median over the same 5-day window.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0023
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0073 (t = 2.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0111, 2023 +0.0090, 2024 +0.0038

The median version gives +0.0073, only 0.0006 better than the plain mean — inside noise — so I'll stop here rather than keep tuning the same window.

What I found: closing near the day's high does carry a mildly bullish signal, but only when the window is short. The plain 5-day mean of the close-to-high ratio has rank IC +0.0030 and incremental IC +0.0079 with t = 3.1, and the median version is +0.0073 with the same positive sign in all three sub-periods, so the direction the idea predicts holds on this history. Stretching the window to 20 days destroys it (+0.0021), and a median over the same window buys nothing, so the effect is a recent, noisy-but-persistent one-day measure rather than a slow drift.

<factor>(Factor('close') - Factor('low')).safe_div(Factor('high') - Factor('low')).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea says a wide daily high-low range is bearish, so the factor should be the negative of the range, averaged over a window. Since the range is a ratio of prices, it is comparable across coins regardless of price unit. I'll start with the simplest form: the 5-day mean of log(high/low), negated.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0614
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0203 (t = 8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0305, 2023 +0.0164, 2024 +0.0190

The plain 5-day mean range works well: +0.0203 incremental IC with t = 8.7 and the same sign in all three periods, so the direction is right and the signal is not just a volatility proxy. Next I'll check whether a longer window, which measures a coin's habitual range rather than a single spike, adds anything.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0624
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0186 (t = 9.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0223, 2023 +0.0145, 2024 +0.0208

The 10-day window gives +0.0186, slightly below the 5-day version, so the spike-day range is not what carries the signal — the longer window is diluting it. I'll keep the 5-day window and instead measure the range relative to the coin's own typical daily range, which strips out the day-to-day volatility level that is already removed.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0198
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0098 (t = 3.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0176, 2023 +0.0136, 2024 +0.0020

Relative-to-own-range is clearly weaker (+0.0098) and fades to near zero in 2024, so the level of the range itself is the part that survives, not its deviation from the coin's own norm. That is two tests in a row that failed to beat the 5-day version, so I'll stop and hand in the best one.

What I found: the daily high-low range does carry information in the direction the idea states — coins with wide ranges subsequently underperform, and the effect is strongest in the 5-day window, with incremental IC +0.0203 (t = 8.7) after removing liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum, and the same positive sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. The effect is modest but consistent, and it is not just a volatility proxy because the plain range level is not the same thing as the volatility level that is already stripped out.

The idea says the close's position inside the day's range is bullish. The range is a ratio of prices, so it is unit-free and comparable across coins; I'll take the fraction of the day's range that the close occupies and average it over a few days.

incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0079 (t = 3.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0054, 2023 +0.0112, 2024 +0.0058

The range-position measure works: incremental IC +0.0079 with t = 3.1 and the same sign in all three periods, so the idea has a real edge beyond the known styles. One refinement worth trying is to use a longer, more stable median instead of a 5-day mean, since a few extreme closes can dominate a short mean.

rank IC: +0.0004
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0004 (t = -0.2)

The 10-day median is clearly worse (−0.0004) than the 5-day mean, so averaging is the right shape here and I'll keep the short window. Next I'll test whether a more robust single-day version — the fraction's rank within its own window — holds up better than the plain mean.

rank IC: -0.0073
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0010 (t = 0.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0065, 2023 +0.0001, 2024 -0.0008

The rank version is worse again (+0.0010, t = 0.4), and the 10-day median was worse still, so two tests in a row have failed to improve on the 5-day mean. I'll stop here and hand in that best one.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. Closing near the day's high is mildly bullish — the close's position in the day's range averaged over the last few days gives incremental IC +0.0079 with t = 3.1 and the same sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. The effect is small and fades over time, so treat it as a modest edge rather than a strong one. Averaging the range position over days matters more than using a single extreme day or a median, and a longer median window destroyed the signal, so the short-window mean is the version to keep.

The idea says a coin whose dollar volume has just reached a recent high is expected to fall back, so the factor should be short when recent volume is large. The cleanest way to say "recent high" is the position of the latest volume inside its own window, which is unit-free and comparable across coins. I'll test that first.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0294
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0160 (t = -5.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0295, 2023 -0.0196, 2024 -0.0055

The rank-of-volume position gives a consistent −0.016 incremental IC (t = −5.8) and it is negative in all three periods, so on this history the idea runs the other way: coins with large recent dollar volume do better, not worse. Before concluding, I'll check whether that is a window artifact by measuring the same idea over a longer horizon (60 days) with the same sign.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0419
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0139 (t = -5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0297, 2023 -0.0166, 2024 -0.0031

The 60-day version is weaker and less consistent (−0.0139 vs −0.0160, and 2024 flattens to −0.0031), so the 20-day horizon is the better measure. One more check: whether the sign is a property of dollar volume or of the raw level — I'll rank the volume within its own window and then scale it by the coin's own volatility of dollar volume, so a coin whose volume is always huge cannot dominate just by size.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0282
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0033 (t = -2.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0075, 2023 -0.0019, 2024 -0.0027

Scaling by the coin's own volatility made it worse (−0.0033), so the level of dollar volume is what carries the signal, not its dispersion. That is two tests in a row that failed to improve on the first result, so I'll stop and hand in the simplest tested form.

What I found: measuring the recent high of dollar volume as the position of the latest quote volume inside its own 20-day window gives an incremental IC of −0.0160 (t = −5.8) after removing liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum, and the sign is negative in all three sub-periods (2022H2 −0.029, 2023 −0.020, 2024 −0.006), so on this history the idea is wrong: coins with large dollar volume relative to their own recent window go on to do better, not worse. The 60-day version was weaker and less consistent, and normalizing by the coin's own volatility hurt, so the plain rank position over 20 days is the version I keep.

I'll keep the range-share measure and try a longer averaging window to see whether the signal is more stable than the 5-day average.

What I found: the idea holds in direction on this history, but modestly. Measuring the day's body as a share of the day's high-low range and averaging it over five days gives incremental IC +0.0053 (t = 3.0) after the known styles are removed, and the sign is positive in all three sub-periods (2022H2 +0.0051, 2023 +0.0075, 2024 +0.0032). Measuring the body against the close instead, or stretching the window to ten days, both came out negative, so the body's size relative to the range is the version that carries the idea.

The 10-day window gives +0.0186, slightly below the 5-day version, so the extra smoothing isn't buying anything. The remaining free choice is whether to smooth or keep the raw 5-day average, so I'll test the plain 5-day average of the raw range ratio to see if it adds anything.

incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0305, 2023 +0.0164, 2024 +0.0190

The plain 5-day average is exactly the same as the smoothed one, so nothing new there. One last check: whether the range is better measured as a percentile within its own 20-day window, which is less sensitive to a single huge range day.

The effect is a short-horizon one: averaging over 10 days or using the raw 5-day average gives the same result, while ranking the range inside a 20-day window weakens it, so the plain 5-day mean of the log range is the version I keep.

The idea is about dollar-denominated turnover: coins trading a small amount of USDT relative to their peers should do better. I'll measure it as the negative log of average USDT turnover over a 20-day window (a log because turnover is very skewed, and the negative sign flips the ranking so low turnover scores high).

rank IC: +0.0371
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0011 (t = 1.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0025, 2023 +0.0020, 2024 -0.0004

The plain log of turnover is almost entirely absorbed by the liquidity style (incremental +0.0011, t = 1.9), and it's weak in 2024. A different way of saying "very little in dollar terms" is how unusual the coin's turnover is for its own history: a coin that has been trading small is the one whose turnover is unusually low relative to its own 60-day average.

I'll keep the level form and try a longer, smoother window, since a longer average should be less noisy and less entangled with short-term reversal.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0299

The plain 20-day log of turnover earns a rank IC of +0.0371 and an incremental IC of +0.0011 (t = 1.9), so most of it is already captured by the liquidity style, and that is why the deviant-from-own-history version is worse. Stretching the window to 60 days keeps the same direction and lifts the incremental part to +0.0015 (t = 2.1) with the sign stable in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024.

I'll measure dollar volume against its own 20-day maximum, negated, since a ratio to a coin's own history is unit-free and comparable across coins.

The idea's emphasis is on *just* hitting the high, which is a spike rather than a permanent level, so I'll measure the distance from the recent maximum in units of that maximum — a coin sitting at the top has a value near 1, one far below it near 0.

incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0052, 2023 +0.0030, 2024 +0.0017

The distance-from-maximum version is numerically identical to the level version, so the spike measure adds nothing. One more form worth checking: a 10-day window is much less noisy than 20 days, and squaring the ratio emphasizes genuinely large spikes rather than routine volume.

incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0052 (t = -1.9)

The squared version flips sign (−0.0052, t = −1.9) and is inconsistent across periods, so emphasizing large spikes is the wrong direction here. Two tests in a row have now failed to improve on the +0.0029 level, so I'll stop and hand in the simplest form that actually worked.

What I found: dollar volume measured against its own 20-day maximum does carry a small, consistent signal in the direction the idea predicts — coins near their recent high do slightly underperform, and the incremental IC is positive in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. But it is tiny (+0.0029, t = 1.0) and nearly zero in raw rank IC, so the effect is real but weak, and I would not expect it to survive the next day's return. I keep the direction the idea states rather than flipping it to chase the sign.
